questions.question:
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series?

15, 27, 12, ?, 9, 33
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is: 

Here, two series are going simultaneously, 

One is, 15, 12, 9 and other is 27, ?, 33

In the first series, 3 is subtracted from the number to get the next number of the series.

15 - 3 = 12, 12 - 3 = 9

And in the second series, 3 is added to the number to get the next number of the series.

27 + 3 = __30__, 30 + 3 = 33

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2aca490b96d5a9bfb0096e27d7f55edaf80aa6e3b2fa39b15f23e8464b16f119.png] 

Hence,** '30' **will replace the question mark in the above series.

questions.question:
Which of the following numbers will replace the question mark (?) in the given series?

13, 14, 23, 48, 97, 178, ?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is: 

Addition of the square of the odd number to previous number to get next number in the series.

13 + **1²** =13 + 1 = 14

14 +** 3****²** = 14 + 9 = **23**

23 +** 5²** = 23 + 25 =** 48 **

48 + **7²** = 48 + 49 = **97** 

97 + **9²** = 97 + 81 = **178**

178 + **11²** = 178 + 121 = **299** 

Hence, the correct option is** 299**

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the third term in the same way as the second term is related to the first term and the sixth term is related to the fifth term.

16 : 69 :: 24 : ? :: 31 : 144
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Logic : (First number × 5) - 11 = Second number**

• 16 : 69

⇒ (16 × 5) - 11

⇒ 80 - 11 = 69

• 31 : 144

⇒ (31 × 5) - 11 

⇒ 155 - 11 = 144

Similarly, 24 : ?

⇒ (24 × 5) - 11

⇒ 120 - 11 = **109**

Hence,** '109'** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
If A denotes ‘+’, B denotes ‘×’, C denotes ‘−’ and D denotes ‘÷’, then what will come in place of ‘?’ in the following equation?

(13 B 9) D 3 A (14 D 7) B 6 C 21 A (32 B 2) = ?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

The BODMAS rule :

 [IMAGE: https://lh6.googleusercontent.com/eeyATaWEJcD1zHnhSk9qsMHdLPgGLd_IlVB_rcJRo7iIkm43j23Ozmk0A-oLNdtx2vVwK6Va50sQEG6d-sHD4rGfiZoc7C9POlEqbfKFyfRu8I1YPXby9Lig-lwDyPKwLkFYWZ_Nb7a7XqMTN6Lt2olAoFhC3Vrxsv2ebItf6rky1udXfbbwuSDw5E4x] 

Decoding the information, 

 
 

 
 
Sign

 
 
 
A

 
 
 
B

 
 
 
C

 
 
 
D

 
 
 

 
 
Means

 
 
 
+

 
 
 
×

 
 
 
-

 
 
 
÷

 
 
 

The given equation is -

(13 **B** 9) **D** 3 **A** (14** D** 7) **B** 6 **C** 21 **A** (32 **B** 2) 

**A **denotes** ‘+’, B **denotes** ‘×’, C **denotes** ‘−’ and D **denotes** ‘÷’**

(13 × 9) ÷ 3 + (14 ÷ 7) × 6 **-** 21 + (32 × 2) 

= __**(13 **____**×**____** 9)**__ ÷ 3 + __**(14 **____**÷**____** 7)**__ × 6 - 21 + __**(32 **____**× 2)**__

= **__117 __**÷**__ 3__** **+** 2 × 6 - 21 **+**** **64 

= 39 + __**2 × 6**__ - 21 + 64 

= __**39 + **12__ - 21 + 64 

=** 51** - 21 **+ 64**

= 115 - 21

= **94**

Hence, **94** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Three statements are given, followed by three conclusions numbered I, II and III. Assuming the statements to be true, even if they seem to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements**:

Some butters are honeys.

Some honeys are breads.

All breads are jams.

**Conclusions**:

I. Some jams are honeys.

II. All honeys are butters.

III. Some jams are butters.

options.text: Only conclusions I and II follow
Only conclusions I and III follow

questions.solution:
**The least possible Venn diagram is as follows:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4599b11687761e09d5c3fcdbe650e9655d4fed5c66341e47c26920ae2e18389a.png] 

**Conclusions:**

I. Some jams are honeys → **True** (Since all breads are jams and some honeys are breads)

II. All honeys are butters → False (It is possible but not definite)

III. Some jams are butters → False (It is possible but not definite)

Hence, **only conclusion 1 follows**.

questions.question: If 21st June 2007 was a Thursday, then what was the day of the week on 21st June 2011 ?
questions.solution:
Given : 21st June 2007 was a Thursday

 
• Total number of days in a normal year = 365 days
 
• Number of odd days in a normal year = 365/7 = 1 day
 
• Total number of days in a leap year = 366 days
 
• Number of odd days in a leap year = 366/7 = 2 days
 
• 21st June 2011 = Thursday + 2 (2008) + 1(2009) + 1(2010) + 1(2011) = Thursday + 5 odd days = Tuesday

Hence, 21st June 2011 held on** Tuesday**.

questions.question: The second number in the given number pairs is obtained by performing certain mathematical operation(s) on the first number. The same operation(s) are followed in all the number pairs, EXCEPT one. Find that odd number pair.
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

**Logic : Difference between first and second number is 29.**

1) 361 : 332 ⇒ 361 - 332 = 29

2) 533 : 504 ⇒ 533 - 504 = 29

3) 440 : 411 ⇒ 440 - 411 = 29

4) 520 : 481 ⇒ 520 - 481 =** 39 ≠ 29**

Hence, **"520 : 481"** is the odd one out.
